claims: Artemis II is a 10-day crewed mission.
Artemis II is scheduled to launch no earlier than April 2026.
Per recent April 1, 2026 updates, Artemis II launched on April 1, 2026.
Artemis II launches on the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket.
Artemis II launches from Kennedy Space Center.
Artemis II will test the Orion spacecraft with four astronauts.
Artemis II marks the first human return to the moon's vicinity since 1972.
SLS places the crew in an initial high-Earth orbit for testing during Artemis II launch.
On Day 1 of Artemis II, Orion performs a manual, human-piloted proximity operations test (Proximity Operations Demonstration).
On Days 2–4 of Artemis II, the service module fires for a translunar injection (TLI).
On Days 2–4 of Artemis II, the translunar injection places the craft on a figure-eight trajectory toward the Moon.
On Days 5–6 of Artemis II, the crew travels roughly 4,600 miles beyond the lunar far side.
On Days 5–6 of Artemis II, the crew uses the lunar far side for a gravity-assisted return.
On Days 5–6 of Artemis II, the crew takes photos of the lunar far side.
On Days 7–9 of Artemis II, the crew transits back to Earth.
On Day 10 of Artemis II, the crew module separates from the service module.
On Day 10 of Artemis II, the crew module enters the atmosphere at 3,000∘F.
On Day 10 of Artemis II, the crew module lands in the Pacific Ocean with a parachute-assisted splashdown.
Reid Wiseman (NASA) is Commander for Artemis II.
Victor Glover (NASA) is Pilot for Artemis II.
Christina Koch (NASA) is Mission Specialist for Artemis II.
Jeremy Hansen (CSA) is Mission Specialist for Artemis II.
